000
FXUS62 KRAH 122312
AFDRAH

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
712 PM EDT Sat Sep 12 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

* No major changes

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 240 PM Saturday...

1) A warm and humid day today, with afternoon showers and another 
round of showers/thunderstorms later tonight. 

2) Limited chances of a shower or storm Sunday afternoon and Sunday 
night, with the greatest chances during the afternoon across the 
Coastal Plain. 

3) A northeast flow will result in near average temperatures and 
lower humidity on Tuesday and Wednesday that will feel cooler than 
recent days.

4) The low and mid level flow will become more east and 
southeasterly late in the work week and weekend resulting in warming 
temperatures, an increase in humidity, and an uptick in rain 
chances. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 240 PM Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... A warm and humid day today, with afternoon showers 
and another round of showers/thunderstorms later tonight.

Last night into this morning, a boundary set up over central NC, 
bisecting the region in half. Shower activity started developing 
along this boundary as it started lifting north over Wake county 
just after noon. PWs over the region are very high (around 2-2.3 in) 
which will allow showers to be efficient rain producers this 
afternoon. This will combine with slow cell motions to create an 
isolated flooding threat, especially if a shower moves over an urban 
or poor drainage area. The area of any showers/thunderstorms should 
increase over the next few hours as the boundary continues north and 
outflows from previous showers/storms provides additional areas of 
lift. 

Later this evening into tonight, an additional area of 
shower/thunderstorm development may be possible as a pre-frontal 
trough moves through central NC from the west. Any rain that 
develops due to this should move faster than this afternoon's rain, 
leading to a lower flooding threat. 

In terms of the strength of the cells today, severe weather is not 
currently expected. CAPE values this afternoon look to maximize 
around 1500-2000 J/kg, with low shear values. This should allow for 
a few cells to get tall enough to produce lightning, but keep any 
winds with them below severe strength. However, a few water-loaded 
downdrafts could produce brief periods of strong gusty winds this 
afternoon. 


KEY MESSAGE 2... Limited chances of a shower or storm Sunday 
afternoon and Sunday night, with the greatest chances during the 
afternoon across the Coastal Plain.

A mid level short wave trough across TN and AL at midday today will 
be located just east of the Blue Ridge on Sunday morning and then 
move offshore by Sunday evening. The best forcing for ascent will be 
east of this feature and should be exiting our eastern areas during 
the afternoon. Deep layer moisture will be above average areawide on 
Sunday but greatest across the east. Expect Sunday to be less 
convectively active than today with the greatest threat of a shower 
or storm across the east during the afternoon. However, a cold front 
will trail behind the short wave trough and move across the area 
late Sunday night and there is a limited chance or a shower or storm 
in the lingering moisture ahead of the front on Sunday night. Highs 
should range in the upper 80s to lower 90s with lows near 70. 


KEY MESSAGE 3... A northeast flow will result in near average 
temperatures and lower humidity on Tuesday and Wednesday that will 
feel cooler than recent days.

An anomalously strong mid-level ridge centered in the TN Valley on 
Tuesday and Wednesday will result in a northerly flow at mid levels 
across VA and the Carolinas while a 1030 mb surface high pressure 
system centered over New England will produce a northeast low level 
flow across the area. The result will be near to slightly above 
seasonal temperatures that will feel notably cooler than recent 
weeks. Highs should range in the lower to mid 80s both days and 
nighttime lows in the lower to mid 60s with some upper 50s (maybe 
mid 50s) possible in the typically cooler locations. Dry weather 
with partly cloudy skies and a noticeable northeast breeze at times 
are expected during the period. 


KEY MESSAGE 4... The low and mid level flow will become more east 
and southeasterly late in the work week and weekend resulting in 
warming temperatures, an increase in humidity, and an uptick in rain 
chances. 

The upper-level ridge at mid levels weakens late in the week and 
becomes more west to east oriented as a mid level weakness/upper low 
organizes near the Bahamas and shifts west into the northern Gulf. 
Meanwhile the narrow surface ridge extending southwest into VA and 
the Carolinas weakens late in the work week as a weak coastal front 
tries to develop off the Carolina coast. The result for our area 
will be an increase in temperatures, moisture and clouds and 
depending on the track and evolution of the upper low and coastal 
font, an uptick in rain chances over the weekend that could increase 
further early next week. 

&&

.AVIATION /00Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
As of 710 PM Saturday...

24 hour TAF period: Scattered showers and a few storms will be 
possible through this evening and into tonight as a weak surface low 
lifts across the area ahead of an approaching cold front. Some 
reduced vsbys and breezy conditions will be possible with the 
showers/storms. Due to increased boundary layer moisture, there 
could be a period of IFR to perhaps LIFR ceilings and/or sub-VFR 
visibilities late tonight/early Sunday morning. Confidence on how 
far east and until when the convection will last is low, and thus so 
is the timing and development of sub-VFR cigs/vsbys east of the 
convection. Restrictions may remain in place until the front moves 
through central NC Sunday afternoon. There will be a limited risk of 
shower/storm development along the frontal passage Sunday afternoon 
into the evening.

Outlook: There will be a non-zero chance of low stratus and/or fog 
development again on Monday morning. VFR conditions are then 
generally expected to prevail. 

&&

.RAH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Blaes/LH 
AVIATION...10/LH
